content.text: This is a classic OWASP Benchmark path traversal test case: tainted parameter flows directly to FileOutputStream without any sanitization.

input.justification: The request parameter "BenchmarkTest01330" is read from request.getParameterMap(), passed through a trivial inner-class method (Test.doSomething) that always returns the tainted value unmodified (the condition (500/42)+196>200 is always true), concatenated with a constant directory path, and used directly to construct a java.io.File / FileOutputStream. There is no validation, canonicalization, or allow-listing of the value before it reaches the file system sink, so an attacker-controlled value can include path traversal sequences (e.g., ../../) to write files outside the intended directory. This matches the known OWASP Benchmark path-injection test pattern and is a true positive.
